title: Conceptual Modeling and Artiﬁcial Intelligence: Mutual Benefits from Complementary Worlds
venue: ER 2021 / CMAI'2021 (3rd International Workshop on Conceptual Modeling Meets Artificial Intelligence)
extended_summary:
This paper is an editorial preface for the 3rd International Workshop on Conceptual Modeling Meets Artificial Intelligence (CMAI'2021). Rather than reporting an empirical study in education, it frames the workshop theme and argues that conceptual modeling and AI can mutually benefit one another. The paper contrasts conceptual modeling’s human-interpretable, explicit, and reproducible representations with AI’s data-driven pattern discovery and black-box predictions, emphasizing complementary strengths and weaknesses.

The paper proposes a research framework that positions conceptual modeling and artificial intelligence orthogonally and defines four research categories: exaptation CMAI, CM-driven CMAI, AI-driven CMAI, and CM- & AI-driven CMAI. It briefly summarizes the invited workshop papers and maps each to this framework, illustrating how conceptual modeling can support machine learning and how AI can contribute to conceptual modeling.

The context is a software engineering / information systems research workshop held with ER 2021, not a K-12 educational intervention. No participant population, implementation setting, or outcome measures are reported. The main conclusion is conceptual and programmatic: the field needs more integrative work that combines explicit modeling with AI methods to improve comprehensibility, development, and application of AI systems.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an editorial preface and workshop overview, not an empirical study. It does not present a research design, sample, or outcome evaluation, so it does not provide evidence meeting research credibility criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: No student, teacher, or institutional outcomes are evaluated. The paper is conceptual and descriptive, so there is no measurable impact estimate to classify.
